name: Chola Empire

areaKm2.note: Educated guess. The world_1000 Chola Empire polygon measures 0.32 million km2 on the sphere (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/master/geojson/world_1000.geojson, low); by 1030 Rajendra also held northern Sri Lanka and Gangavadi and had Vengi as a vassal, hence the mid and high.

population.note: Educated guess. No estimate found. HYDE puts all of India at 112.5M in 1000 and Sri Lanka at 0.8M (OWID https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/population.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true); Maddison (via the Delhi Sultanate page) has ~75M for India up to 1000. The Chola core (Tamil country, Gangavadi, northern Sri Lanka) is ~8-10% of the subcontinent; Vengi was a vassal.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Temple towns (Thanjavur, Kanchipuram) and ports; mostly rural Kaveri delta.

activePersonnel.note: Educated guess. Standing regiments only (feudatory levies in trainedReserves). A Western Chalukya inscription accuses Rajendra of leading 955,000 men, and Chola-side tradition gives 900,000 at Maski (1020) (Rajendra I page): enemy and court claims, rejected. Mid ~1.2% of population.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Feudatory contingents and temple-assigned levies.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Mahouts (2-3 per elephant), ship crews (~40 per ship), engineers and commissariat.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Standing regiments plus feudatory and temple-assigned levies.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Kaikkolar and other named regiments listed in the Tanjavur inscriptions (Imperial Chola Army page).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: era-typical South Indian infantry

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: standing regiments with royal titles

count.note: Educated guess. Villigal archer regiments (Imperial Chola Army page).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: long bows

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: standing regiments

count.note: Educated guess. Kudiraichchevagar cavalry regiments mounted on imported Arabian horses.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: imported horses, scarce

count.note: Educated guess. Elephant corps (Perundanattu Anaiyatkal); Rajendra's armoured elephants were central to his campaigns (War elephant page). Later Chinese claims of tens of thousands are not used.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: armoured war elephants

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: royal stables

count.note: Educated guess. Expeditionary shipping for Sri Lanka, the Maldives and the 1025 Srivijaya raid. Subbarayalu (2009, Chola dynasty page bibliography) argues there was no standing navy; ships were largely requisitioned merchant vessels.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: merchant-type sea-going ships

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: experienced merchant crews

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.75 (proven commanders). Evidence: Rajendra I beat the Chalukyas at Maski (1020), marched to the Ganges (1019-21) and raided Srivijaya (1025)

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.5-0.75. Evidence: named standing regiments with royal identity

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75 (recent victories). Evidence: unbroken run of campaigns 1012-1025

weapons.note: Anchor: between 3 and 4. Evidence: swords, spears, long bows; armoured elephants

armor.note: Anchor: about 3. Evidence: quilted and mail armour for elites only

ships.note: Anchor: 3. Evidence: sea-going trading ships able to reach Sumatra and Kedah

fortification.note: Anchor: 3. Evidence: walled temple cities and forts

logistics.note: Anchor: 3. Evidence: Kaveri irrigation surplus, river and coastal transport

communications.note: Anchor: 3. Evidence: royal orders inscribed in temple records; courier system

isr.note: Anchor: 3. Evidence: merchant-guild intelligence across the Bay of Bengal

gdpPerCapita.note: Analogue: Maddison 2023 (via OWID grapher CSV, https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-maddison-project-database.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true) has India only from 1600 (1,264) and China 1000 = 1,225, 1150 = 1,181; Egypt 1000 = 956, 1300 = 972 (2011 int$). Medieval South Asia placed in that band.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Standing regiments and plunder-financed campaigns.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Bronze casting, textiles, temple construction.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Irrigated Kaveri delta rice.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the classical snapshots.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Royal highways (peruvazhi) linking temple towns.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Nagapattinam, Kaveripattinam, Mamallapuram, Thondi.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Merchant guild fleets (Ainnurruvar) trading to China and Southeast Asia.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. The Ganges expedition marched ~1,500 km but foraged and was supplied by vassals.

homeDefense.note: 1.1-1.2 row: familiar terrain, temple-fortress cities, monsoon.

notes: Snapshot 1030, late in Rajendra I's reign, after the Ganges expedition and the 1025 Srivijaya raid. Army numbers in inscriptions (900,000, 955,000) are court and enemy claims and are not used; all force counts are educated guesses. The Chola navy is disputed: Subbarayalu argues the state kept no permanent navy, so ships are small, requisitioned platforms. Population convention: Chola-ruled lands only (Vengi and Srivijaya excluded). Border: world_1000 is the nearest file at or before 1030 containing the polity; it shows only the core. Personnel: active = the standing named regiments, elephant corps and expedition shipping; trainedReserves = feudatory, hill-tribe and temple levies; mobilizable = population x ratio.
